title: Rensselaer County Sheriff's Office Flock network request reconciliation
summary: Request #1901 preserves the reported eight-camera county Flock network, the Poestenkill site-agreement and DCJS-funding lead, and the unresolved NYSDOT correspondence conflict while keeping municipal and private-site systems separate.

sources.title: Residents question proposal for automatic license plate reader at Poestenkill intersection

data.question: What public evidence currently establishes the Rensselaer County Sheriff's Office Flock network and its relationship to locality/private-site proposals?
data.method: Reconciled the existing canonical county targets with November 2025 Times Union reporting and current first-party Sheriff's Office context.
data.framework: County-owned cameras, municipal police networks, approved locality placements, rejected proposals, and private-property proposals remain separate network/ownership states unless evidence links them.
data.scope: Public Rensselaer County Sheriff's Office ALPR network, proposals, funding lead, and named public officials; no private-person enrichment.
findings: November 2025 independent reporting states county law enforcement had placed eight Flock cameras across Rensselaer County.
Sheriff Kyle Bourgault and Capt. Justin Walraed presented the Poestenkill proposal at the Nov. 13 Town Board meeting, with the agency primarily seeking a revocable site agreement.
The proposed Poestenkill camera was reported as funded through the New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services.

Walraed reported difficulty obtaining NYSDOT approval for camera placements nearer heavily traveled state routes, while NYSDOT separately told the Times Union it had received no government request to install cameras in or around Poestenkill.
Petersburgh, Greenbush municipal systems, Troy, and proposed Stewart's private-property placements are not folded into the eight-camera county inventory absent ownership evidence.
conclusions: An eight-camera county Flock deployment is independently reported, but the serial-level inventory, ownership chain, contracts, exact grant award, users, audits, and sharing graph remain unresolved.
The NYSDOT statements constitute an unresolved records/correspondence question rather than a basis to accuse either side of misrepresentation.
recommendations: Recover exact DCJS award and county acceptance/budget records plus contracts, purchase orders, invoices, renewals, maintenance, and site agreements.
Recover the eight-camera serial/location/lifecycle inventory and Organization Audit, Network Audit, SharedNetworks, event logs, users/admins, and configuration exports.
Recover NYSDOT and Sheriff's Office correspondence sufficient to reconcile the placement-approval statements.
counterarguments: The phrase 'county law enforcement has placed eight Flock cameras' does not identify each asset, owner, site, or administrative account.
NYSDOT's statement was scoped to requests in or around Poestenkill and does not resolve whether other county placement requests were submitted.
limitations: No native contract, DCJS award notice, NYSDOT correspondence, camera inventory, or Flock platform export was recovered in this pass.
unresolved: Where are the eight county cameras and who owns and maintains each one?
What exact DCJS award and procurement instruments funded the network or proposed expansion?
Who administers the network and what directed sharing edges exist?
What correspondence explains the NYSDOT placement-approval discrepancy?

title: Auto-Dig request #1901 Rensselaer Sheriff network pass
summary: Queue-first request pass reuses four existing Rensselaer County targets and records the eight-camera county lead, Poestenkill site/funding evidence, and unresolved NYSDOT correspondence boundary.

data.research_question: What portion of request #1901 can be advanced now without duplicating existing Rensselaer County target identities?
data.method: Read the request and comments, reused four existing canonical Rensselaer investigation targets, and reconciled the reported county deployment, Poestenkill proposal/funding, named officials, and NYSDOT statement.
classification_rules: Reuse stable canonical IDs when materially equivalent targets already exist.
County, municipal, and private-property systems remain separate absent ownership evidence.
A funding lead is not an exact grant award until native award/procurement records are recovered.
Conflicting or differently scoped public statements are preserved as unresolved evidence rather than flattened.

findings.finding: Four existing canonical Rensselaer targets cover the camera inventory, contracts/grants, sharing network, and audit exports and were reused.
Eight county Flock cameras were independently reported by November 2025.
The Poestenkill proposal supplies a reported DCJS funding lead and identifies Sheriff Kyle Bourgault and Capt. Justin Walraed in the placement chain.
The NYSDOT statement leaves the exact placement-request correspondence unresolved.
